transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi… yeah, thank you. I guess I’m here because flying has been feeling a lot scarier than I think it should. Even just thinking about getting on a plane, I kind of go right back to this bad turbulence we had on my honeymoon flight. I know, logically, people fly safely all the time, so I feel a little silly saying it, but it’s been bothering me enough that I thought I should talk to someone.
Outside of flying, do you often feel excessive worry about many other parts of your life?

Um… I don’t think so, not really. I mean, I worry about normal stuff like work or family things, but it doesn’t feel excessive or constant. It’s mostly the flying that feels… out of proportion, I guess. Does that make sense?
During that turbulence on your honeymoon flight, did you think you might die?

I’m… not totally sure. In the moment it felt really terrifying, like my body reacted as if something awful could happen, but I don’t know if I had the clear thought of, “I’m going to die.” It was more like panic and wanting it to stop, if that makes sense.
Do you have unwanted flashbacks of that turbulence episode?

I don’t think I’d call them flashbacks, exactly. Like, I can remember it really clearly if I start thinking about flying, but it’s not like I’m suddenly back there without warning… at least I don’t think so. Is that what you mean?
Do you avoid flying because of this fear?

Yeah… I guess I do. I mean, I try not to make a big deal out of it, but I’ve definitely chosen long drives instead of flying, and I’ve turned down some work trainings if getting there meant I’d have to fly.

And even just talking about a trip, if it seems like flying might be involved, I kind of need my husband there with me or I start wanting to back out. I know that probably sounds silly, but… yeah, I do avoid it.
During that turbulence, did it feel like your life was in danger?

I’m not sure I can say it that clearly. It definitely felt unsafe, like something was wrong and I wanted it to be over immediately. But I don’t know if I was thinking, “my life is in danger,” exactly… maybe my body felt that way more than my mind did. Does that make sense?
Have you ever suddenly felt as if you were back on that honeymoon flight, like it was happening again in the moment?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I can picture it if I’m talking about flying or thinking about it, but I haven’t had moments where I suddenly feel like I’m actually back on that plane. At least, not that I’ve noticed. Is that the kind of thing you mean?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a circumscribed, disproportionate fear focused on flying, with clear avoidance behavior and reliance on her husband when air travel is anticipated. Worry is not generalized to multiple domains, and the interview does not support PTSD because there is no clearly qualifying traumatic stressor with perceived life threat, no flashbacks, and no re-experiencing episodes. The presentation is most consistent with specific phobia, situational type (flying).
